Interviewer: Moving to present time, tell me more about family who are important to you. Do you have a partner, or children?

Agent: Currently, I am single and do not have children. However, I am very close to my sister who lives nearby, and we see each other frequently.

Interviewer: Are there anyone else in your immediate family whom you have not mentioned? Who are they, and what is your relationship with them like?

Agent: Aside from my parents who still live in my hometown, I have a few cousins I'm close to, even though we don’t see each other often. We maintain a strong connection through regular phone calls and social media.

Interviewer: Tell me about anyone else in your life we haven't discussed (like friends or romantic partners). Are there people outside of your family who are important to you?

Agent: Outside of my family, I have a close-knit group of friends from college, and we make it a point to meet at least once a year. My lifelong friend, Jenna, is like a sibling to me, and we often catch up for hiking trips whenever possible. Also, I am part of a community gardening club where I've formed lasting friendships based on mutual interests.

Agent: I live with my partner and our two kids. My partner works from home, and the kids are in school during weekdays.

Interviewer: Is there anyone who usually lives here but is away - traveling, at school, or in a hospital?

Agent: No, there is no one who usually lives here but is currently away.

Interviewer: Living any place has its ups and downs. Tell me about what it's been like for you living here.

Agent: Living here has been a wonderful experience for me. I enjoy the cultural diversity and the endless opportunities to learn and engage with different communities. However, like any city, it has its downsides, such as the noise and occasional traffic hassle. Nonetheless, the positives far outweigh the negatives for me.

Interviewer: If you have children, tell me about a typical weekday during the school year for your children. What is their daily routine? And what are after school activities your children participate in?

Agent: I don't have children, so there is no school year routine in my household.

Interviewer: At what kind of job or jobs do you work, and when do you work?

Agent: I work full-time as a software engineer at a tech company. My work hours are 9 AM to 5 PM, Monday through Friday.

Interviewer: At what kind of job or jobs do you work, and when do you work?

Agent: I work full-time as a software engineer at a tech company. My work hours are 9 AM to 5 PM, Monday through Friday.

Interviewer: One topic a lot of people have been talking about recently is race and/or racism and policing. Some tell us issues raised by the Black Lives Matter movement have affected them a lot, some say they've affected them somewhat, others say they haven't affected them at all. How about for you?

Agent: The issues raised by the Black Lives Matter movement have affected me somewhat. They've prompted me to reflect more on the systemic issues within policing and society.

Interviewer: Have you or your immediate family ever used alternative forms of medicine? This might include indigenous, non-western, or informal forms of care.

Agent: I haven't extensively used alternative medicine, but I have tried herbal teas for relaxation and chamomile for better sleep.

Interviewer: Tell me a story about a time in the last year when you were in a rough place or struggling emotionally.

Agent: Last year, there was a time when I felt overwhelmed with work and personal responsibilities. I managed to get through it by talking to friends and focusing on one task at a time.

Interviewer: Tell me about any recent changes in your political views.

Agent: Recently, I've become more aware of environmental issues and have shifted towards supporting policies that address climate change more aggressively.

Interviewer: Tell me about any time during the past year that you haven't had enough money to buy something that you needed or pay a bill that was due.

Agent: There was one instance last year when I couldn't afford an unexpected car repair right away, but I managed to cover it after adjusting my budget.

Interviewer: Now we're going to talk a bit more about what life was like for you over the past year. Tell me all about how you have been feeling.

Agent: Over the past year, I've had a mixture of emotions. I've experienced stress due to changes in my routine but also found joy in small things and personal growth.

Agent: People I'm close to have generally been proactive; many have attended local protests or participated in community discussions.

Agent: I occasionally experience anxiety, particularly during stressful situations, but I manage it with mindfulness techniques and exercise.

Agent: My family has been resilient, supporting each other through regular video calls and shared activities at home, even though it's been challenging at times.

Agent: I use platforms like Instagram and LinkedIn to stay updated, follow interesting content, and maintain professional connections.

Agent: Yes, I use Facebook groups and Twitter to seek advice and support during challenging periods.

Agent: I worked 48 weeks in the past year, including my vacation time.

Agent: Last year, my income was especially low during the summer months due to reduced freelance opportunities. To make ends meet, I took a part-time job at a local bookstore, cut down on non-essential expenses, and utilized a small emergency fund to cover necessary bills.

Agent: I've been at my current job for 2 years. The benefits are decent, including health insurance, paid time off, and vacation days.

Agent: My work schedule is somewhat predictable, but there is some flexibility in adjusting hours if needed.
